claims.claim: PG&E occupies a physical grid bottleneck between growing electricity demand and reliable delivery; data-center demand can increase infrastructure utilization, while sensors, smart-meter data and machine learning can reduce ignition and outage risk.

The >12 GW data-center pipeline is a demand signal rather than realized load; conversion depends on interconnection, generation, transmission, tariffs, permitting and affordability, making those successor bottlenecks central to scenario robustness.

risks.risk: Wildfire exposure is a persistent physical-system externality that can overwhelm financial benefits if mitigation fails.

unknowns.unknown: Firm contractual status, timing and realized economics of the >12 GW pipeline remain unestablished in cited evidence.

falsifiers: Material failure of mitigation investments to reduce ignition/outage severity would weaken the resilience edge.
Low conversion of the announced load pipeline after required infrastructure spending would weaken the demand-utilization thesis.

claims.claim: Current undergrounding, covered-line and monitoring milestones are constructive execution evidence but do not eliminate wildfire tail risk or determine future regulatory treatment.

Large-load growth is not automatically beneficial to shareholders or customers; financing costs, tariff design, capital recovery and affordability determine whether infrastructure expansion creates durable value.

risks.risk: Wildfire liabilities and extreme-event severity remain high-impact tail risks.
Regulatory recovery and financing costs can erode returns from required grid investment.
Pipeline headline size can overstate realized demand if projects are delayed, resized or cancelled.

unknowns.unknown: Current sources do not establish future wildfire-loss distribution, final tariff treatment, financing mix or contracted pipeline conversion.
